hypothesis: Added a RankNet-style pairwise logistic ranking loss on r_close over the near band (trading-day offsets 1-5), weighted at 0.01 alongside the existing smooth-L1 regression, because rank_ic_near is invariant to monotone transforms of the prediction while squared error spends model capacity on the unforecastable return level -- training the model to order names rather than to hit their magnitudes should directly raise the ranking metric it is scored on.

Shortened the training response block from 90 to 20 forecast days, because the causal within-block mask makes offsets 1-5 identical at either size while the 70 dropped far-horizon tokens are essentially unforecastable noise that consumes gradient, mask-token capacity, and prefix context -- training on a horizon the model can actually resolve, with a 70-day-longer feature prefix, should sharpen the near-band cross-sectional ordering that rank_ic_near measures.

Added an exponential moving average (decay 0.999) of the model weights that is swapped in for every validation pass -- so the monitored val_rank_ic_near and the saved best.ckpt are both the averaged iterate -- and swapped back out before the next training batch, leaving the optimization trajectory itself untouched; because daily cross-sectional return signal has a very low signal-to-noise ratio the late-training iterate random-walks inside a wide basin instead of converging (visible as the baseline's 0.068-0.145 single-seed spread), and Polyak averaging cancels the signal-uncorrelated gradient-noise component of the final weights, which should raise the 3-seed mean rank_ic_near by lifting the typical seed and shrinking the spread.

Tripled the validation sample per pass (50 -> 150 batches) and halved the pass frequency (every 500 -> 1000 steps), because best.ckpt is the argmax of a noisy 50-batch val_rank_ic_near estimate over ~20 draws -- a winner's-curse selection that saves the checkpoint that got lucky on validation rather than the one that generalizes -- so a lower-variance selection statistic evaluated fewer times should pick a genuinely better iterate and raise the mean rank_ic_near while shrinking the 0.068-0.145 seed spread.

Raised the streaming dataset's live-streamer cache from 8 to 32 (= BATCH_SIZE), because StockHandlerDataset draws every window in a batch from only cache_size concurrently-open stocks and drains each stock before replacing it, so a 32-sample batch currently holds ~4 temporally-adjacent windows from each of just 8 tickers -- gradients are strongly correlated in both name and date, inflating gradient noise and plausibly driving the 0.068-0.145 seed spread; giving each batch ~32 distinct names decorrelates the minibatch (and makes it resemble the cross-section the metric is computed over) at zero extra compute per step, which should lift the typical seed's rank_ic_near and shrink the spread.
